summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple sclerosis, neurogenic bladder, and chronic left hip osteomyelitis, was admitted for fatigue and chills. He was found to have Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia and urinary tract infection, along with Enterococcus in the urine. He was initially treated with vancomycin and cefepime, then transitioned to piperacillin-tazobactam after a PICC line was placed. Blood cultures cleared, and his white count normalized. Iron studies revealed iron deficiency anemia, and he was started on oral iron and a bowel regimen. The doxycycline for chronic osteomyelitis was not restarted per infectious disease recommendation. He was discharged home with visiting nursing services to complete a 14-day course of IV antibiotics and continue wound and medication management.
